text.p: Turkish central bank stepped in to counter a severe cash shortage faced by banks on Wednesday due to a 134.4 trillion lira auction payment to the treasury and a 47.7 trillion lira repo repayment to the central bank, bankers said.
The central bank injected 46 trillion lira at an average yield of 111.13 percent by opening a new repo auction with one-week maturity in the morning.

The bank also made overnight repo deals earlier in the day day to feed cash and prevent the overnight repo rates from rising above 80 percent, bankers said. The average overnight repo rate ended sharply higher at 79.31 percent, versus Tuesday's 65.62 percent.
The central bank lent banks 5.5 trillion lira at 72 percent on overnight, six trillion lira at 71 percent via tom/next and 900 billion lira at 72 percent via tom/week.
The average overnight money rate also soared to 71.80 percent from Tuesday's 55.19.
Bond yields continued their rise amid tight liquidity and strong sales by a private bank holding a heavy portfolio of May 13, 1998 bills sold in last week's treasury auction.
Bankers said heavy sales in May 13 paper caused yields to climb across the board by around two percentage points.
The most heavily traded papers were May 13 and June 10, 1998 which yielded 106.45 and 106.12 percent, respectively, up 2.19 and 2.12 percentage points from Tuesday.
Bankers said price rises by the new government since the beginning of this week prompted expectations of higher inflation and unnerved the market.

Taxes on Turkish petroleum products were raised by 20 and 90 percentage points on Monday, leading to price increases of 15 and 32 percent in products. Tolls on highways and Bosphorus bridges were also raised by between 100 and 150 percent on Wednesday.
State Minister Gunes Taner who is in charge of economy, has said the price hikes would lead to higher inflation in the next few months.
Turkish lira eased slightly to 153,880 to the dollar from Tuesday's 153,800 close in line with the dollar/mark parity.
A minor gap has come up since Tuesday between the central bank's key dollar rate and banks' dollar bids as the U.S. currency rose sharply rose against mark.
